paragraph: Bergenfield's single-family market is the whole story here: 67 sales over six months at a median of $699,000, with a sale-to-list ratio of 1.045, nearly 75 percent of homes selling above asking, and a median of 19 days on market. That is a real seller's market, and buyers should expect competition on the good ones. The typical sale is a three-bedroom colonial, cape, or split-level with two full baths, though prices run from $395,000 up to $1,750,000, so the median is the number to anchor on. The monthly series tracks the usual seasonal arc, with the median peaking at $812,500 in June and settling to $650,000 in July while closings rose to 15, the busiest month of the window. That combination points to a mix shift toward smaller homes rather than falling values. Multi-family is thin at 6 sales, median $745,000, almost all legal two-families, and those sellers are seeing closer to list than the single-family crowd. If you are weighing the two, the deciding factor is whether you want a house to live in or rental income carrying part of the payment.
